out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Cannot Exceed 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item for which time rather than temperature is being used as a control was not cooked, served or discarded by the expiration time as indicated: OBSERVED BEAN SPROUTS ON TIME MOVED TO A REFRIGERATOR WHEN TIMEFRAME HAD ENDED.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours is used as the public health control : 1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature or, 2) the food shall have an initial temperature of 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 3) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 4) the food shall be cooked and served, served if ready to eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 5) the food if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit shall be discarded. EHS REVIEWED TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL WITH THE STAFF. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS ON TIME ARE DISCARDED OF AFTER THE 4-HOUR TIMEFRAME.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: OBSERVED LARGE BATCHES OF FROZEN RAW BEEF SITTING ON COUNTER-TOP TO THAW.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS REVIEWED PROPER THAWING METHODS WITH THE PIC. PIC MOVED BEEF TO THE WALK-IN COOLER. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED SCOOPS IN BOTH ICE MACHINES WITH HANDLES DOWN/IN THE ICE.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC PLACED SCOOPS HANDLE UPRIGHT DURING INSPECTION. PHO VIET FRESH (Inspection Date: 04/09/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Safe Materials
violations.observation: OBSERVED A LARGE WOODEN POLE PURCHASED FROM A HARDWARE STORE USED TO STIR BROTH AT GRILL-LINE.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be safe. PIC REMOVED POLE DURING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS ONLY FOOD- GRADE EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS SHOULD BE USED FOR COOKING.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: OBSERVED INTERIOR/EXTERIOR OF REFRIGERATION UNITS (ESPECIALLY THE TWO-DOOR UPR FREEZERS AND THREE-DOOR PREP TOP), SHELVING IN THE WALK-IN COOLER, AND GRILL-LINE EQUIPMENT ARE IN NEED OF CLEANING.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. PLEASE ENSURE THESE AREAS ARE CLEANED THOROUGHLY PRIOR TO FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: OBSERVED HOLE IN CEILING AROUND WATER HEATER.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. PLEASE ENSURE CEILING IS SEALED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the FLOORS/WALLS AROUND THE GRILL-LINE AND NEAR THREE-VAT SINK/DISHWASHING MACHINE is in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. PLEASE THOROUGHLY CLEAN THESE AREAS PRIOR TO FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, Train Employees on Food Safety
violations.observation: Employees are not properly trained in food safety, including food storage organization, handwashing, bare hand contact with ready to eat food, as it relates to their assigned duties.
violations.corrective_action: The Person in Charge or certified food manager shall train all his/her employees in food safety, including allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. PLEASE USE GUIDANCE RESOURCES PREVIOUSLY PROVIDED TO TRAIN STAFF ACCORDINGLY. ENSURE EDUCATION IS PROVIDED TO STAFF BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. OBSERVED NO CFM ONSITE AT BEGINNING OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. CFM CAME DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE THERE IS A CFM ON SITE DURING ALL HOURS OF OPERATION INCLUDING DURING PREPARATION.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' OBSERVED NO EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY SIGNED FOR NEW EMPLOYEES. EHS PREVIOUSLY EMAILED EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY IN SPANISH TO PIC.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE ALL EMPLOYEES REVIEW AND SIGN EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP. MAINTAIN SIGNED COPIES ONSITE FOR REVIEW BY HEALTH DEPARTMENT.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: OBSERVED EMPLOYEE HANDLE COOKED CHICKEN WITH BARE HANDS FROM 3 DOOR PREP-TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD CHICKEN. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: OBSERVED HANDWASH SINK IN SERVICE AREA WITH 2 JUGS OF ICE WATER IN BASIN; OBSERVED HANDWASH SINK NEAR PREP SINK WITH UTENSILS STORED IN BASIN.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REMOVED ITEMS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE HANDSINKS AND OTHER SINKS ARE USED ONLY FOR DESIGNATED PURPOSES. NO ITEMS SHOULD BE STORED IN HANDWASHING SINK BASINS.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: OBSERVED A BOWL OF RAW BEEF STACKED ON TOP OF A CONTAINER OF SCALLOPS IN AVANTCO 3 DOOR PREP TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): OBSERVED GARLIC IN OIL AND CUT LETTUCE ON COUNTER TOP WITHOUT TEMPERATURE CONTROL OR LABELS INDICATING 4 HOUR TIME.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO INCLUDE ITEMS TO THE TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL PROCEDURES AND ADD 4 HOUR TIME LABELS TO GARLIC AND LETTUCE. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: OBSERVED SHAKING BEEF ON MENU NOT IDENTIFIED AS BEING SERVED UNDERCOOKED; PIC INFORMED EHS SHAKING BEEF IS ALWAYS SERVED UNDERCOOKED (COOKED “MEDIUM”).
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE UPDATE MENU TO IDENTIFY SHAKING BEEF AND ANY OTHER FOOD ITEMS WHICH MAY BE SERVED UNDERCOOKED OR RAW BY FOLLOW UP, OR DECIDED TO DISCONTINUE UNDERCOOKING SHAKING BEEF.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED VARIOUS FOOD ITEMS STORED DIRECTLY ON FLOOR UNDER KITCHEN SINK, ON FLOOR OF WALK-IN COOLER, AND THROUGHOUT BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE FOOD ITEMS ARE STORED ON APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS.

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: OBSERVED FROZEN PINEAPPLE AND BEEF BONES STORED UNDER HANDWASH SINK NEAR PREP SINK IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC RELOCATED FOOD ITEMS AWAY FROM CONTAMINATION DURING INSPECTION.

violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: OBSERVED HANDSINK NEAR KITCHEN ENTRANCE WITH NOODLES IN BASIN.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEE COMPLIANCE AT ALL TIMES.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. OBSERVED GRILL CHICKEN AT 57F AND GRILL PORK AT 48F AND GRILLED BEEF AT 45F FOR MORE THAN HOUR ON KITCHEN COUNTER; FISH BROTH AT 45F FOR MORE THAN 8 HOURS IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED ON COOLING TIME AND METHODS. ADDITIONAL GUIDELINES WILL BE FORWARDED BY EMAIL. PLEASE ENSURE COMPLIANCE IS MAINTAINED. PIC DISCARDED FISH BROTH AND MEATS DURING INSPECTION.

violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS WILL FORWARD TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL DOCUMENTATION FOR FOODS IDENTIFIED TO BE MAINTAINED ON TIME. PLEASE ENSURE COMPLIANCE BY FOLLOW UP INSPECTION. out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. OBSERVED CLEANING CHEMICALS STORED WITH FOODS AND UTENSILS UNDER KITCHEN COUNTERS.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC RELOCATED CHEMICALS. PLEASE ENSURE CHEMICALS ARE KEPT IN DESIGNATED AREA AFTER USE, SEPARATED FROM FOODS, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, FOOD SERVICE ITEMS AND LINENS. PHO VIET FRESH (Inspection Date: 11/01/2024) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED FISH BROTH AT 45F COOKED FROM THE DAY BEFORE IN DEEP FOOD STORAGE CONTAINERS WITH LIDS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED ON POSSIBLE METHODS TO COOL BROTH. PIC DISCARDED DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE UTILIZE APPROPRIATE METHODS TO COOL BROTHS WITHIN THE 6 HOUR TIME FRAME DISCUSSED.
